# Usage telemetry

## Task

Capture how the app is used, so the admin can see every interaction with it.
This is a separate log from the domain event log: the event log records what
happened in the job search, and this records what happened in the software.

Every response the API sends is recorded as a row in a `usage` table, written
by middleware after the response, in a short separate transaction so that a
failed request is still logged. A row holds: `id`; `owner_id`, which is empty
for unauthenticated requests; `at`; `client`, one of web, mcp, cli, api or
unknown, taken from a required `X-Client` header that the web app and the MCP
server always send; `session_id`; `route`, the route pattern rather than the
URL; `method`; `status`; `duration_ms`; `entity_type` and `entity_id`, when the
route has an entity; and `tool_name`, the MCP intent tool, when the MCP server
sets an `X-Tool` header.

Page views in the web app are recorded too: `POST /usage/view` takes a route
and an entity id, for the web app to call on navigation.

`GET /admin/usage`, with optional `since`, `owner` and `client` filters, is
for the admin only. It returns the matching rows and a daily summary: active
users, requests by client, intent tools by count, and entity pages by count.
It is served through the admin role, so it crosses tenants on purpose.

Usage rows are kept for 180 days and pruned by a nightly job.

The work is done when a day of mixed web and MCP use is visible per user and
per tool from the admin endpoint.

## Constraints

- No request bodies, no search strings and no document contents are recorded.

## Scope exclusions

- The web app and the MCP server do not exist yet. Making them send the
  headers or call `POST /usage/view` is later work.
- No hosting or scheduler setup for the nightly job.

+"""Record every API response in the usage log (`app.models.usage`).
+
+`UsageMiddleware` wraps the whole app. Once the response has been sent, it
+writes one row in a session of its own, `get_usage_session`, so a request
+that failed or rolled back its own transaction is still logged. A failure to
+write the row is logged and never reaches the caller.
+
+What a row is built from:
+
+- `client` from the `X-Client` header. The web app and the MCP server always
+  send it; a request without it, or with a value not in `UsageClient`, is
+  recorded as `unknown` rather than refused.
+- `session_id` from `X-Session-Id`, and `tool_name` from `X-Tool`, which the
+  MCP server sets to the intent tool it is running.
+- `owner_id` from `authenticate`, which leaves it on the request state.
+- `route` from the matched route's pattern, never the URL.
+- `entity_type` and `entity_id` from a route whose pattern has an `{id}`
+  parameter: the type is the pattern's first segment, e.g. `people` for
+  `/people/{id}`. Entity routes name their id `id` for this.
+
+`POST /usage/view` puts the page it was told about on the request state, and
+the row records that page instead of the call itself.
+"""
+
+import logging
+import time
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from datetime import UTC, datetime
+from typing import Any
+from uuid import UUID, uuid4
+
+import anyio.to_thread
+from sqlalchemy import insert
+from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
+from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send
+
+from app.db import get_engine
+from app.models.usage import VIEW_METHOD, UsageClient, usage
+
+log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+CLIENT_HEADER = b"x-client"
+SESSION_HEADER = b"x-session-id"
+TOOL_HEADER = b"x-tool"
+# Longer header values are cut, so a client cannot make a row arbitrarily big.
+MAX_HEADER_LENGTH = 200
+
+# Keys on the request state (`scope["state"]`).
+OWNER_KEY = "usage_owner_id"
+VIEW_KEY = "usage_view"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PageView:
+    """The web app page that `POST /usage/view` reports."""
+
+    route: str
+    entity_id: UUID | None
+
+
+def get_usage_session() -> Iterator[Session]:
+    """The session the usage row is written in: the database user, committed on its own.
+
+    Overridable like a dependency, through `app.dependency_overrides`.
+    """
+    with Session(get_engine()) as session:
+        yield session
+
+
+def entity_of(route: str | None, entity_id: Any) -> tuple[str | None, UUID | None]:
+    """The entity a route pattern is about, given the value of its `{id}`."""
+    if route is None or "{id}" not in route or entity_id is None:
+        return None, None
+    try:
+        parsed = entity_id if isinstance(entity_id, UUID) else UUID(str(entity_id))
+    except ValueError:
+        return None, None
+    return route.strip("/").split("/")[0], parsed
+
+
+def page_entity(route: str, entity_id: UUID | None) -> tuple[str | None, UUID | None]:
+    """The entity a web app page is about: its first segment, when it has an id."""
+    if entity_id is None:
+        return None, None
+    return route.strip("/").split("/")[0] or None, entity_id
+
+
+def _header(scope: Scope, name: bytes) -> str | None:
+    for key, value in scope["headers"]:
+        if key == name:
+            text: str = value.decode("latin-1")[:MAX_HEADER_LENGTH]
+            return text or None
+    return None
+
+
+def _client(scope: Scope) -> UsageClient:
+    value = (_header(scope, CLIENT_HEADER) or "").strip().lower()
+    return UsageClient(value) if value in UsageClient else UsageClient.unknown
+
+
+def build_row(scope: Scope, status: int, duration_ms: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    state: dict[str, Any] = scope.get("state", {})
+    view: PageView | None = state.get(VIEW_KEY)
+    if view is not None:
+        route: str | None = view.route
+        method = VIEW_METHOD
+        entity_type, entity_id = page_entity(view.route, view.entity_id)
+    else:
+        matched = scope.get("route")
+        route = getattr(matched, "path", None)
+        method = scope["method"]
+        entity_type, entity_id = entity_of(route, scope.get("path_params", {}).get("id"))
+    return {
+        "id": uuid4(),
+        "owner_id": state.get(OWNER_KEY),
+        "at": datetime.now(UTC),
+        "client": _client(scope).value,
+        "session_id": _header(scope, SESSION_HEADER),
+        "route": route,
+        "method": method,
+        "status": status,
+        "duration_ms": duration_ms,
+        "entity_type": entity_type,
+        "entity_id": entity_id,
+        "tool_name": _header(scope, TOOL_HEADER),
+    }
+
+
+class UsageMiddleware:
+    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp) -> None:
+        self.app = app
+
+    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
+        if scope["type"] != "http":
+            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
+            return
+        started = time.perf_counter()
+        status = 500
+
+        async def capture(message: Message) -> None:
+            nonlocal status
+            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
+                status = message["status"]
+            await send(message)
+
+        try:
+            await self.app(scope, receive, capture)
+        finally:
+            duration_ms = round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
+            row = build_row(scope, status, duration_ms)
+            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(_write, scope, row)
+
+
+def _write(scope: Scope, row: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    app = scope.get("app")
+    overrides = getattr(app, "dependency_overrides", {})
+    factory = overrides.get(get_usage_session, get_usage_session)
+    try:
+        sessions = factory()
+        session = next(sessions)
+        try:
+            session.execute(insert(usage).values(row))
+            session.commit()
+        finally:
+            sessions.close()
+    except Exception:
+        log.exception("Could not record usage for %s %s", row["method"], row["route"])

+"""Page views in the web app, which calls `POST /usage/view` on navigation.
+
+The call writes nothing itself: it tells `app.usage` which page to record, and
+the usage row for this request records that page instead of the call.
+"""
+
+from uuid import UUID
+
+from fastapi import APIRouter, Request, Response, status
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+from app.auth import CurrentPrincipal
+from app.usage import VIEW_KEY, PageView
+
+router = APIRouter(prefix="/usage", tags=["usage"])
+
+
+class PageViewIn(BaseModel):
+    # The page's route pattern, e.g. `/people/:id`. A query string or fragment
+    # is dropped, so no search string is recorded.
+    route: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)
+    entity_id: UUID | None = None
+
+
+@router.post("/view", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
+def record_view(body: PageViewIn, request: Request, principal: CurrentPrincipal) -> Response:
+    route = body.route.split("?", 1)[0].split("#", 1)[0]
+    setattr(request.state, VIEW_KEY, PageView(route=route, entity_id=body.entity_id))
+    return Response(status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)

+class UsageRow(BaseModel):
+    id: UUID
+    owner_id: UUID | None
+    at: datetime
+    client: UsageClient
+    session_id: str | None
+    route: str | None
+    method: str
+    status: int
+    duration_ms: int
+    entity_type: str | None
+    entity_id: UUID | None
+    tool_name: str | None
+
+
+class EntityPageCount(BaseModel):
+    entity_type: str
+    entity_id: UUID
+    views: int
+
+
+class UsageDay(BaseModel):
+    """One UTC day of the matching rows."""
+
+    day: date
+    active_users: int
+    requests_by_owner: dict[UUID, int]
+    requests_by_client: dict[UsageClient, int]
+    tools_by_count: dict[str, int]
+    entity_pages_by_count: list[EntityPageCount]
+
+
+class UsageReport(BaseModel):
+    rows: list[UsageRow]
+    days: list[UsageDay]
+
+
+AdminSession = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_admin_session)]
+
+
+@router.get("/usage", dependencies=[Depends(require_admin)])
+def usage_report(
+    session: AdminSession,
+    since: datetime | None = None,
+    owner: UUID | None = None,
+    client: UsageClient | None = None,
+    limit: Annotated[int, Query(ge=1, le=10_000)] = 1000,
+) -> UsageReport:
+    conditions: list[ColumnElement[bool]] = []
+    if since is not None:
+        conditions.append(usage.c.at >= since)
+    if owner is not None:
+        conditions.append(usage.c.owner_id == owner)
+    if client is not None:
+        conditions.append(usage.c.client == client.value)
+    where = and_(True, *conditions)
+
+    rows = session.execute(
+        select(usage).where(where).order_by(usage.c.at.desc()).limit(limit)
+    ).mappings()
+    return UsageReport(
+        rows=[UsageRow.model_validate(dict(row)) for row in rows],
+        days=_days(session, where),
+    )
+
+
+def _days(session: Session, where: ColumnElement[bool]) -> list[UsageDay]:
+    day = func.date(func.timezone("UTC", usage.c.at)).label("day")
+    days: dict[date, UsageDay] = {}
+
+    def on(value: date) -> UsageDay:
+        if value not in days:
+            days[value] = UsageDay(
+                day=value,
+                active_users=0,
+                requests_by_owner={},
+                requests_by_client={},
+                tools_by_count={},
+                entity_pages_by_count=[],
+            )
+        return days[value]
+
+    def grouped(*columns: Any, extra: ColumnElement[bool] | None = None) -> Any:
+        query = select(day, *columns, func.count().label("n")).where(where)
+        if extra is not None:
+            query = query.where(extra)
+        return session.execute(query.group_by(day, *columns))
+
+    for value, owner_id, n in grouped(usage.c.owner_id, extra=usage.c.owner_id.is_not(None)):
+        on(value).requests_by_owner[owner_id] = n
+        on(value).active_users += 1
+    for value, client, n in grouped(usage.c.client):
+        on(value).requests_by_client[UsageClient(client)] = n
+    for value, tool, n in grouped(usage.c.tool_name, extra=usage.c.tool_name.is_not(None)):
+        on(value).tools_by_count[tool] = n
+    pages = and_(usage.c.method == VIEW_METHOD, usage.c.entity_id.is_not(None))
+    for value, entity_type, entity_id, n in grouped(
+        usage.c.entity_type, usage.c.entity_id, extra=pages
+    ):
+        on(value).entity_pages_by_count.append(
+            EntityPageCount(entity_type=entity_type, entity_id=entity_id, views=n)
+        )
+    for summary in days.values():
+        summary.entity_pages_by_count.sort(key=lambda page: -page.views)
+    return [days[value] for value in sorted(days, reverse=True)]

    connection: Connection, db_session: Session
) -> None:

+"""The usage log: what happened in the software, one row per API response.
+
+This is not the domain event log, which records what happened in the job
+search. It has no Pydantic model and is not in `TABLES`: nothing in the domain
+reads or writes it. `app.usage` writes it, as the database user; only the
+admin role can read it, for `GET /admin/usage`.
+
+No request bodies, search strings or document contents go in it. `route` is
+the route pattern, never the URL, so a query string cannot reach it.
+"""
+
+from enum import StrEnum
+
+from sqlalchemy import CheckConstraint, Column, DateTime, ForeignKey, Index, Integer, Table, Text
+from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import UUID as PgUUID
+
+from app.db import Base
+
+
+class UsageClient(StrEnum):
+    """Which client made the request, from the `X-Client` header."""
+
+    web = "web"
+    mcp = "mcp"
+    cli = "cli"
+    api = "api"
+    unknown = "unknown"
+
+
+# A page view in the web app, recorded by `POST /usage/view`, has this method.
+VIEW_METHOD = "VIEW"
+
+CLIENT_VALUES = ", ".join(f"'{client.value}'" for client in UsageClient)
+
+usage = Table(
+    "usage",
+    Base.metadata,
+    Column("id", PgUUID(as_uuid=True), primary_key=True),
+    # Null for a request that never authenticated.
+    Column("owner_id", PgUUID(as_uuid=True), ForeignKey("owners.id"), nullable=True),
+    Column("at", DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False),
+    Column("client", Text(), nullable=False),
+    Column("session_id", Text(), nullable=True),
+    # Null when no route matched, so an unknown URL is never recorded.
+    Column("route", Text(), nullable=True),
+    Column("method", Text(), nullable=False),
+    Column("status", Integer(), nullable=False),
+    Column("duration_ms", Integer(), nullable=False),
+    Column("entity_type", Text(), nullable=True),
+    Column("entity_id", PgUUID(as_uuid=True), nullable=True),
+    Column("tool_name", Text(), nullable=True),
+    CheckConstraint(f'"client" IN ({CLIENT_VALUES})', name="client_values"),
+    Index("ix_usage_at", "at"),
+    Index("ix_usage_owner_id_at", "owner_id", "at"),
+)

+"""Record every API response in the usage log (`app.models.usage`).
+
+`UsageMiddleware` wraps the whole app. Once the response has been sent, it
+writes one row in a session of its own, `get_usage_session`, so a request
+that failed or rolled back its own transaction is still logged. A failure to
+write the row is logged and never reaches the caller.
+
+What a row is built from:
+
+- `client` from the `X-Client` header. The web app and the MCP server always
+  send it; a request without it, or with a value not in `UsageClient`, is
+  recorded as `unknown` rather than refused.
+- `session_id` from `X-Session-Id`, and `tool_name` from `X-Tool`, which the
+  MCP server sets to the intent tool it is running.
+- `owner_id` from `authenticate`, which leaves it on the request state.
+- `route` from the matched route's pattern, never the URL.
+- `entity_type` and `entity_id` from a route whose pattern has an `{id}`
+  parameter: the type is the pattern's first segment, e.g. `people` for
+  `/people/{id}`. Entity routes name their id `id` for this.
+
+`POST /usage/view` puts the page it was told about on the request state, and
+the row records that page instead of the call itself.
+"""
+
+import logging
+import time
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from datetime import UTC, datetime
+from typing import Any
+from uuid import UUID, uuid4
+
+import anyio.to_thread
+from sqlalchemy import insert
+from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
+from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send
+
+from app.db import get_engine
+from app.models.usage import VIEW_METHOD, UsageClient, usage
+
+log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+CLIENT_HEADER = b"x-client"
+SESSION_HEADER = b"x-session-id"
+TOOL_HEADER = b"x-tool"
+# Longer header values are cut, so a client cannot make a row arbitrarily big.
+MAX_HEADER_LENGTH = 200
+
+# Keys on the request state (`scope["state"]`).
+OWNER_KEY = "usage_owner_id"
+VIEW_KEY = "usage_view"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PageView:
+    """The web app page that `POST /usage/view` reports."""
+
+    route: str
+    entity_id: UUID | None
+
+
+def get_usage_session() -> Iterator[Session]:
+    """The session the usage row is written in: the database user, committed on its own.
+
+    Overridable like a dependency, through `app.dependency_overrides`.
+    """
+    with Session(get_engine()) as session:
+        yield session
+
+
+def entity_of(route: str | None, entity_id: Any) -> tuple[str | None, UUID | None]:
+    """The entity a route pattern is about, given the value of its `{id}`."""
+    if route is None or "{id}" not in route or entity_id is None:
+        return None, None
+    try:
+        parsed = entity_id if isinstance(entity_id, UUID) else UUID(str(entity_id))
+    except ValueError:
+        return None, None
+    return route.strip("/").split("/")[0], parsed
+
+
+def page_entity(route: str, entity_id: UUID | None) -> tuple[str | None, UUID | None]:
+    """The entity a web app page is about: its first segment, when it has an id."""
+    if entity_id is None:
+        return None, None
+    return route.strip("/").split("/")[0] or None, entity_id
+
+
+def _header(scope: Scope, name: bytes) -> str | None:
+    for key, value in scope["headers"]:
+        if key == name:
+            text: str = value.decode("latin-1")[:MAX_HEADER_LENGTH]
+            return text or None
+    return None
+
+
+def _client(scope: Scope) -> UsageClient:
+    value = (_header(scope, CLIENT_HEADER) or "").strip().lower()
+    return UsageClient(value) if value in UsageClient else UsageClient.unknown
+
+
+def build_row(scope: Scope, status: int, duration_ms: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    state: dict[str, Any] = scope.get("state", {})
+    view: PageView | None = state.get(VIEW_KEY)
+    if view is not None:
+        route: str | None = view.route
+        method = VIEW_METHOD
+        entity_type, entity_id = page_entity(view.route, view.entity_id)
+    else:
+        matched = scope.get("route")
+        route = getattr(matched, "path", None)
+        method = scope["method"]
+        entity_type, entity_id = entity_of(route, scope.get("path_params", {}).get("id"))
+    return {
+        "id": uuid4(),
+        "owner_id": state.get(OWNER_KEY),
+        "at": datetime.now(UTC),
+        "client": _client(scope).value,
+        "session_id": _header(scope, SESSION_HEADER),
+        "route": route,
+        "method": method,
+        "status": status,
+        "duration_ms": duration_ms,
+        "entity_type": entity_type,
+        "entity_id": entity_id,
+        "tool_name": _header(scope, TOOL_HEADER),
+    }
+
+
+class UsageMiddleware:
+    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp) -> None:
+        self.app = app
+
+    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
+        if scope["type"] != "http":
+            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
+            return
+        started = time.perf_counter()
+        status = 500
+
+        async def capture(message: Message) -> None:
+            nonlocal status
+            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
+                status = message["status"]
+            await send(message)
+
+        try:
+            await self.app(scope, receive, capture)
+        finally:
+            duration_ms = round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
+            row = build_row(scope, status, duration_ms)
+            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(_write, scope, row)
+
+
+def _write(scope: Scope, row: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    app = scope.get("app")
+    overrides = getattr(app, "dependency_overrides", {})
+    factory = overrides.get(get_usage_session, get_usage_session)
+    try:
+        sessions = factory()
+        session = next(sessions)
+        try:
+            session.execute(insert(usage).values(row))
+            session.commit()
+        finally:
+            sessions.close()
+    except Exception:
+        log.exception("Could not record usage for %s %s", row["method"], row["route"])

+"""Record every API response in the usage log (`app.models.usage`).
+
+`UsageMiddleware` wraps the whole app. Once the response has been sent, it
+writes one row in a session of its own, `get_usage_session`, so a request
+that failed or rolled back its own transaction is still logged. A failure to
+write the row is logged and never reaches the caller.
+
+What a row is built from:
+
+- `client` from the `X-Client` header. The web app and the MCP server always
+  send it; a request without it, or with a value not in `UsageClient`, is
+  recorded as `unknown` rather than refused.
+- `session_id` from `X-Session-Id`, and `tool_name` from `X-Tool`, which the
+  MCP server sets to the intent tool it is running.
+- `owner_id` from `authenticate`, which leaves it on the request state.
+- `route` from the matched route's pattern, never the URL.
+- `entity_type` and `entity_id` from a route whose pattern has an `{id}`
+  parameter: the type is the pattern's first segment, e.g. `people` for
+  `/people/{id}`. Entity routes name their id `id` for this.
+
+`POST /usage/view` puts the page it was told about on the request state, and
+the row records that page instead of the call itself.
+"""
+

+import time
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from datetime import UTC, datetime
+from typing import Any
+from uuid import UUID, uuid4
+

+from sqlalchemy import insert

+from app.models.usage import VIEW_METHOD, UsageClient, usage

+SESSION_HEADER = b"x-session-id"
+TOOL_HEADER = b"x-tool"

+MAX_HEADER_LENGTH = 200
+
+# Keys on the request state (`scope["state"]`).
+OWNER_KEY = "usage_owner_id"
+VIEW_KEY = "usage_view"

+class PageView:
+    """The web app page that `POST /usage/view` reports."""
+
+    route: str
+    entity_id: UUID | None
+
+
+def get_usage_session() -> Iterator[Session]:
+    """The session the usage row is written in: the database user, committed on its own.
+
+    Overridable like a dependency, through `app.dependency_overrides`.
+    """
+    with Session(get_engine()) as session:
+        yield session
+
+
+def entity_of(route: str | None, entity_id: Any) -> tuple[str | None, UUID | None]:
+    """The entity a route pattern is about, given the value of its `{id}`."""
+    if route is None or "{id}" not in route or entity_id is None:
+        return None, None
+    try:
+        parsed = entity_id if isinstance(entity_id, UUID) else UUID(str(entity_id))
+    except ValueError:
+        return None, None
+    return route.strip("/").split("/")[0], parsed
+
+
+def page_entity(route: str, entity_id: UUID | None) -> tuple[str | None, UUID | None]:
+    """The entity a web app page is about: its first segment, when it has an id."""
+    if entity_id is None:
+        return None, None
+    return route.strip("/").split("/")[0] or None, entity_id
+
+
+def _header(scope: Scope, name: bytes) -> str | None:
+    for key, value in scope["headers"]:
+        if key == name:
+            text: str = value.decode("latin-1")[:MAX_HEADER_LENGTH]
+            return text or None
+    return None
+

+def _client(scope: Scope) -> UsageClient:
+    value = (_header(scope, CLIENT_HEADER) or "").strip().lower()
+    return UsageClient(value) if value in UsageClient else UsageClient.unknown
+
+
+def build_row(scope: Scope, status: int, duration_ms: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    state: dict[str, Any] = scope.get("state", {})
+    view: PageView | None = state.get(VIEW_KEY)
+    if view is not None:
+        route: str | None = view.route
+        method = VIEW_METHOD
+        entity_type, entity_id = page_entity(view.route, view.entity_id)
+    else:
+        matched = scope.get("route")
+        route = getattr(matched, "path", None)
+        method = scope["method"]
+        entity_type, entity_id = entity_of(route, scope.get("path_params", {}).get("id"))
+    return {
+        "id": uuid4(),
+        "owner_id": state.get(OWNER_KEY),
+        "at": datetime.now(UTC),
+        "client": _client(scope).value,
+        "session_id": _header(scope, SESSION_HEADER),
+        "route": route,
+        "method": method,
+        "status": status,
+        "duration_ms": duration_ms,
+        "entity_type": entity_type,
+        "entity_id": entity_id,
+        "tool_name": _header(scope, TOOL_HEADER),

+        status = 500

+"""Page views in the web app, which calls `POST /usage/view` on navigation.
+
+The call writes nothing itself: it tells `app.usage` which page to record, and
+the usage row for this request records that page instead of the call.
+"""
+
+from uuid import UUID
+
+from fastapi import APIRouter, Request, Response, status
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+from app.auth import CurrentPrincipal
+from app.usage import VIEW_KEY, PageView
+
+router = APIRouter(prefix="/usage", tags=["usage"])
+
+
+class PageViewIn(BaseModel):
+    # The page's route pattern, e.g. `/people/:id`. A query string or fragment
+    # is dropped, so no search string is recorded.
+    route: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)
+    entity_id: UUID | None = None
+
+
+@router.post("/view", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
+def record_view(body: PageViewIn, request: Request, principal: CurrentPrincipal) -> Response:
+    route = body.route.split("?", 1)[0].split("#", 1)[0]
+    setattr(request.state, VIEW_KEY, PageView(route=route, entity_id=body.entity_id))
+    return Response(status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)

+"""Record every API response in the usage log (`app.models.usage`).
+
+`UsageMiddleware` wraps the whole app. Once the response has been sent, it
+writes one row in a session of its own, `get_usage_session`, so a request
+that failed or rolled back its own transaction is still logged. A failure to
+write the row is logged and never reaches the caller.
+
+What a row is built from:
+
+- `client` from the `X-Client` header. The web app and the MCP server always
+  send it; a request without it, or with a value not in `UsageClient`, is
+  recorded as `unknown` rather than refused.
+- `session_id` from `X-Session-Id`, and `tool_name` from `X-Tool`, which the
+  MCP server sets to the intent tool it is running.
+- `owner_id` from `authenticate`, which leaves it on the request state.
+- `route` from the matched route's pattern, never the URL.
+- `entity_type` and `entity_id` from a route whose pattern has an `{id}`
+  parameter: the type is the pattern's first segment, e.g. `people` for
+  `/people/{id}`. Entity routes name their id `id` for this.
+
+`POST /usage/view` puts the page it was told about on the request state, and
+the row records that page instead of the call itself.
+"""
+
+import logging
+import time
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from datetime import UTC, datetime
+from typing import Any
+from uuid import UUID, uuid4
+
+import anyio.to_thread
+from sqlalchemy import insert
+from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
+from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send
+
+from app.db import get_engine
+from app.models.usage import VIEW_METHOD, UsageClient, usage
+
+log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+CLIENT_HEADER = b"x-client"
+SESSION_HEADER = b"x-session-id"
+TOOL_HEADER = b"x-tool"
+# Longer header values are cut, so a client cannot make a row arbitrarily big.
+MAX_HEADER_LENGTH = 200
+
+# Keys on the request state (`scope["state"]`).
+OWNER_KEY = "usage_owner_id"
+VIEW_KEY = "usage_view"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PageView:
+    """The web app page that `POST /usage/view` reports."""
+
+    route: str
+    entity_id: UUID | None
+
+
+def get_usage_session() -> Iterator[Session]:
+    """The session the usage row is written in: the database user, committed on its own.
+
+    Overridable like a dependency, through `app.dependency_overrides`.
+    """
+    with Session(get_engine()) as session:
+        yield session
+
+
+def entity_of(route: str | None, entity_id: Any) -> tuple[str | None, UUID | None]:
+    """The entity a route pattern is about, given the value of its `{id}`."""
+    if route is None or "{id}" not in route or entity_id is None:
+        return None, None
+    try:
+        parsed = entity_id if isinstance(entity_id, UUID) else UUID(str(entity_id))
+    except ValueError:
+        return None, None
+    return route.strip("/").split("/")[0], parsed
+
+
+def page_entity(route: str, entity_id: UUID | None) -> tuple[str | None, UUID | None]:
+    """The entity a web app page is about: its first segment, when it has an id."""
+    if entity_id is None:
+        return None, None
+    return route.strip("/").split("/")[0] or None, entity_id
+
+
+def _header(scope: Scope, name: bytes) -> str | None:
+    for key, value in scope["headers"]:
+        if key == name:
+            text: str = value.decode("latin-1")[:MAX_HEADER_LENGTH]
+            return text or None
+    return None
+
+
+def _client(scope: Scope) -> UsageClient:
+    value = (_header(scope, CLIENT_HEADER) or "").strip().lower()
+    return UsageClient(value) if value in UsageClient else UsageClient.unknown
+
+
+def build_row(scope: Scope, status: int, duration_ms: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    state: dict[str, Any] = scope.get("state", {})
+    view: PageView | None = state.get(VIEW_KEY)
+    if view is not None:
+        route: str | None = view.route
+        method = VIEW_METHOD
+        entity_type, entity_id = page_entity(view.route, view.entity_id)
+    else:
+        matched = scope.get("route")
+        route = getattr(matched, "path", None)
+        method = scope["method"]
+        entity_type, entity_id = entity_of(route, scope.get("path_params", {}).get("id"))
+    return {
+        "id": uuid4(),
+        "owner_id": state.get(OWNER_KEY),
+        "at": datetime.now(UTC),
+        "client": _client(scope).value,
+        "session_id": _header(scope, SESSION_HEADER),
+        "route": route,
+        "method": method,
+        "status": status,
+        "duration_ms": duration_ms,
+        "entity_type": entity_type,
+        "entity_id": entity_id,
+        "tool_name": _header(scope, TOOL_HEADER),
+    }
+
+
+class UsageMiddleware:
+    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp) -> None:
+        self.app = app
+
+    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
+        if scope["type"] != "http":
+            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
+            return
+        started = time.perf_counter()
+        status = 500
+
+        async def capture(message: Message) -> None:
+            nonlocal status
+            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
+                status = message["status"]
+            await send(message)
+
+        try:
+            await self.app(scope, receive, capture)
+        finally:
+            duration_ms = round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
+            row = build_row(scope, status, duration_ms)
+            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(_write, scope, row)
+
+
+def _write(scope: Scope, row: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    app = scope.get("app")
+    overrides = getattr(app, "dependency_overrides", {})
+    factory = overrides.get(get_usage_session, get_usage_session)
+    try:
+        sessions = factory()
+        session = next(sessions)
+        try:
+            session.execute(insert(usage).values(row))
+            session.commit()
+        finally:
+            sessions.close()
+    except Exception:
+        log.exception("Could not record usage for %s %s", row["method"], row["route"])

+"""Record every API response in the usage log (`app.models.usage`).
+
+`UsageMiddleware` wraps the whole app. Once the response has been sent, it
+writes one row in a session of its own, `get_usage_session`, so a request
+that failed or rolled back its own transaction is still logged. A failure to
+write the row is logged and never reaches the caller.
+
+What a row is built from:
+
+- `client` from the `X-Client` header. The web app and the MCP server always
+  send it; a request without it, or with a value not in `UsageClient`, is
+  recorded as `unknown` rather than refused.
+- `session_id` from `X-Session-Id`, and `tool_name` from `X-Tool`, which the
+  MCP server sets to the intent tool it is running.
+- `owner_id` from `authenticate`, which leaves it on the request state.
+- `route` from the matched route's pattern, never the URL.
+- `entity_type` and `entity_id` from a route whose pattern has an `{id}`
+  parameter: the type is the pattern's first segment, e.g. `people` for
+  `/people/{id}`. Entity routes name their id `id` for this.
+
+`POST /usage/view` puts the page it was told about on the request state, and
+the row records that page instead of the call itself.
+"""
+
+import logging
+import time
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from datetime import UTC, datetime
+from typing import Any
+from uuid import UUID, uuid4
+
+import anyio.to_thread
+from sqlalchemy import insert
+from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
+from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send
+
+from app.db import get_engine
+from app.models.usage import VIEW_METHOD, UsageClient, usage
+
+log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+CLIENT_HEADER = b"x-client"
+SESSION_HEADER = b"x-session-id"
+TOOL_HEADER = b"x-tool"
+# Longer header values are cut, so a client cannot make a row arbitrarily big.
+MAX_HEADER_LENGTH = 200
+
+# Keys on the request state (`scope["state"]`).
+OWNER_KEY = "usage_owner_id"
+VIEW_KEY = "usage_view"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PageView:
+    """The web app page that `POST /usage/view` reports."""
+
+    route: str
+    entity_id: UUID | None
+
+
+def get_usage_session() -> Iterator[Session]:
+    """The session the usage row is written in: the database user, committed on its own.
+
+    Overridable like a dependency, through `app.dependency_overrides`.
+    """
+    with Session(get_engine()) as session:
+        yield session
+
+
+def entity_of(route: str | None, entity_id: Any) -> tuple[str | None, UUID | None]:
+    """The entity a route pattern is about, given the value of its `{id}`."""
+    if route is None or "{id}" not in route or entity_id is None:
+        return None, None
+    try:
+        parsed = entity_id if isinstance(entity_id, UUID) else UUID(str(entity_id))
+    except ValueError:
+        return None, None
+    return route.strip("/").split("/")[0], parsed
+
+
+def page_entity(route: str, entity_id: UUID | None) -> tuple[str | None, UUID | None]:
+    """The entity a web app page is about: its first segment, when it has an id."""
+    if entity_id is None:
+        return None, None
+    return route.strip("/").split("/")[0] or None, entity_id
+
+
+def _header(scope: Scope, name: bytes) -> str | None:
+    for key, value in scope["headers"]:
+        if key == name:
+            text: str = value.decode("latin-1")[:MAX_HEADER_LENGTH]
+            return text or None
+    return None
+
+
+def _client(scope: Scope) -> UsageClient:
+    value = (_header(scope, CLIENT_HEADER) or "").strip().lower()
+    return UsageClient(value) if value in UsageClient else UsageClient.unknown
+
+
+def build_row(scope: Scope, status: int, duration_ms: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    state: dict[str, Any] = scope.get("state", {})
+    view: PageView | None = state.get(VIEW_KEY)
+    if view is not None:
+        route: str | None = view.route
+        method = VIEW_METHOD
+        entity_type, entity_id = page_entity(view.route, view.entity_id)
+    else:
+        matched = scope.get("route")
+        route = getattr(matched, "path", None)
+        method = scope["method"]
+        entity_type, entity_id = entity_of(route, scope.get("path_params", {}).get("id"))
+    return {
+        "id": uuid4(),
+        "owner_id": state.get(OWNER_KEY),
+        "at": datetime.now(UTC),
+        "client": _client(scope).value,
+        "session_id": _header(scope, SESSION_HEADER),
+        "route": route,
+        "method": method,
+        "status": status,
+        "duration_ms": duration_ms,
+        "entity_type": entity_type,
+        "entity_id": entity_id,
+        "tool_name": _header(scope, TOOL_HEADER),
+    }
+
+
+class UsageMiddleware:
+    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp) -> None:
+        self.app = app
+
+    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
+        if scope["type"] != "http":
+            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
+            return
+        started = time.perf_counter()
+        status = 500
+
+        async def capture(message: Message) -> None:
+            nonlocal status
+            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
+                status = message["status"]
+            await send(message)
+
+        try:
+            await self.app(scope, receive, capture)
+        finally:
+            duration_ms = round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
+            row = build_row(scope, status, duration_ms)
+            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(_write, scope, row)
+
+
+def _write(scope: Scope, row: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    app = scope.get("app")
+    overrides = getattr(app, "dependency_overrides", {})
+    factory = overrides.get(get_usage_session, get_usage_session)
+    try:
+        sessions = factory()
+        session = next(sessions)
+        try:
+            session.execute(insert(usage).values(row))
+            session.commit()
+        finally:
+            sessions.close()
+    except Exception:
+        log.exception("Could not record usage for %s %s", row["method"], row["route"])
